newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's most famous spy released from prison.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's most famous spy released from prison.

text.p: Swedish spy Stig Bergling, sentenced to life imprisonment in 1979 for passing virtually all of his country's defence plans to Moscow, was freed on Wednesday after serving a total of 11-1/2 years in jail.

His subdued exit from jail lacked the drama of his previous spell of freedom which began in 1987 when he escaped while on an unsupervised conjugal visit. He spent seven years on the run abroad before surrendering to Swedish police, saying he was homesick.
"Things could not be better on such a beautiful morning. Eleven and a half years wears a person down a bit," Bergling told reporters as he left a prison south of Stockholm.
Bergling, who was born in 1937, did not know what he would do but he hoped to be allowed to remain in Sweden.
A former senior security police officer, Bergling was found guilty of spying for the Soviet Union for almost a decade.
At the time of his escape, he had been married to Elisabeth Sandberg, a mother of four, for less than a year. Sandberg, who died of cancer earlier this year, had helped him plan his escape.

Bergling's sentence was reduced to 23 years in the spring of 1996 but last November Swedish authorities said the convicted spy, who suffers from Parkinson's disease, would only have to serve half of this as he was unlikely to return to a life of crime.
